title: 想 / 要 — want to
explanation: 想  means "would like to" (softer desire); 要  means "want to" or "will" (stronger intention). Both come before the verb.

examples.english: I would like to drink water.
Do you want to go to Beijing?

examples.pinyin: wǒ men xiǎng chī zhōng guó cài
examples.english: We would like to eat Chinese food.

examples.pinyin: tā men yào mǎi xīn shǒu jī
examples.english: They want to buy new phones.

notes: 要 can also mean "will" for near-future plans: 我要走了. To negate, use 不想 or 不要 before the verb.
